result.title: MCPGuard: Finding Conformance Gaps in MCP SDKs via Dual-Track Analysis and Dynamic Adjudication
result.summary: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects large language model agents to external tools and services through official SDKs that implement message validation and session logic. Specification constraints omitted by these SDKs may propagate to downstream applications, highlighting the importance of SDK-level conformance testing. Yet existing MCP conformance tools mainly exercise running endpoints and reveal little about whether SDK models enforce specification requirements. We present MCPGuard, an automated LLM-based framework for detecting specification-to-SDK conformance gaps. Its structural track aligns JSON Schema constraints with normalized SDK models and produces constraint-specific evidence. Its behavioral track extracts normative prose rules, retrieves bounded function-level slices, and audits them with LLMs for candidate omissions. An evidence-aware dynamic adjudicator then inspects complete source context and builds PoCs to validate candidates. A shared kernel with language-specific adapters enables analysis across SDKs. On the official Python 1.26.0 and TypeScript 1.29.0 SDKs, MCPGuard confirms 13 and 19 findings, respectively, none of which are exposed by two black-box baselines. Tests on open MCP servers further show that these gaps can systematically propagate downstream. By making SDK conformance of specification constraints directly testable, MCPGuard complements conventional endpoint-oriented conformance suites.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 MCPGuard，一个基于 LLM 的自动化框架，通过结构化模式对齐与行为规范审计的双轨分析加动态裁决，检测 MCP 官方 SDK 相对规范的实现缺口，并在 Python/TypeScript SDK 及开放 MCP 服务器上验证其发现可向下游传播。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究对象是协议 SDK 的规范一致性与软件测试工具链，不涉及 VLM 推理的视觉表示、latent 状态生成、证据使用或停止决策，也未提出可供 LVR 借鉴的状态或计算机制线索，故排除。
